review_notes: [v2] References page, raw extractor output before this review. Rebuilt as heading "## REFERENCES" (was "#") plus 30 text items, one per entry, in printed order [1]-[21] (left column) then [22]-[30] (right column); the extractor had placed [22]-[30] between [9] and [10], had merged [3]+[4], [15]+[16], [23]+[24] into single items and prefixed every entry with a list dash. Entry text was generated from the authors' main.bbl in printed IEEE style ("[n] authors, “title,” *venue*, ...") and then compared per entry, punctuation included, with the native PDF lines (script v2/p7.py): the only differences are fi/fl ligature code points, the three line-wrap hyphens removed (Burgard in [6], autonomous in [7], avoidance in [22]) and the composed "ö" of Blösch in [9]. Compound hyphens at line wraps kept as in the bbl: "Perception-aware" [15], "deep-stall" [27]; page ranges split by a line wrap rejoined ("114–123" [4], "969–1002" [16], "235–250" [29]). TeX versus PDF: the bbl has a U+2010 hyphen in "High-speed" of [17]; the PDF prints an ordinary hyphen, which is used. Entries [4], [9], [16], [19], [20], [22], [27], [30] were also read against the 150 dpi page render. Authors' capitalisation kept as printed (nmpc, uav, mav, 3d, gps-denied, lqr-trees, b-splines). Venue titles are italic as printed. Item ids of the split entries: p0007-b003b ([4]), p0007-b022b ([16]), p0007-b010b ([24]). The right column ends after [30]; the rest of the page is blank. Verifier check: OK.
